Rashi on Gittin 13b:10:1.english: He transferred - [the lender transferred] this loan.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:10:2.hebrew: לנולדים - שזה המקבל נולד לאחר אותה הלואה:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:10:2.english: To those who will be born - For this recipient was born after that loan.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:10:3.hebrew: הכי נמי דלא קנו - דכיון דטעמא משום שעבודא דקביל עליה לוה בשעת הלואה לאישתעבודי להאי דאתי מחמתיה הוא, ואיהו לא היה בעולם בההיא שעתא, לא קני:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:10:3.english: So too, they do not acquire - For since the reason [that the third party acquires] is because of the obligation that the borrower accepted upon himself at the time of the loan, to be obligated to this one who comes by virtue of him [i.e., the lender's creditor], and [the one yet to be born] was not in the world at that time, he does not acquire.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:11:1.hebrew: ואפי' לר' מאיר דאמר אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם - כגון מוכר פירות דקל, או האומר מה שתעלה מצודתי:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:11:1.english: And even according to Rabbi Meir, who says that a person can transfer ownership of an item that has not yet come into the world - For example, one who sells the fruits of a palm tree [that have not yet grown], or [one who says], "Whatever my net brings up [will be yours]."

Rashi on Gittin 13b:11:2.hebrew: הני מילי - כי מקנה לאדם שישנו בעולם, אבל לדבר שאינו בעולם — לא:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:11:2.english: This applies - Only when one transfers ownership to a person who exists in the world; but to an entity that does not [yet] exist in the world — no.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:1:1.hebrew: לא שנא במלוה - ואע"ג דלהוצאה ניתנה ואינה בעין, הלכך לא בעינן צבורין, אי במעמד שלשתן קמיירי המתני':
Rashi on Gittin 13b:1:1.english: It is no different with a loan - Even though it was given to be spent and is not [physically] present, therefore we do not require [the money to be] piled, if the mishna is speaking of [a transfer] in the presence of all three [parties].

Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:1.hebrew: טעמא דמת - הוא דלא יתנו, דאין גט לאחר מיתה:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:1.english: The reason is that he died - That is [the reason] they should not give [it], for there is no divorce after death.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:2.hebrew: הא מחיים נותנין - ולא צריך תו לאימלוכי ביה:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:2.english: But [if he said it] while alive, they give [the get] - And there is no further need to deliberate about it.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:3.hebrew: וטעמא דאמר תנו - כלומר, והא דדייקינן "הא מחיים נותנין" — טעמא דאמר מעיקרא "תנו", כדקתני "תנו גט לאשתי":
Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:3.english: And the reason is that he said "Give" - That is to say, when we inferred, "But if [he died] during his lifetime, they give [the document]" — the reason is that he said at the outset "Give," as [the Mishnah] teaches: "Give a bill of divorce to my wife."

Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:4.hebrew: הא לא אמר תנו - אלא אמר כתבו, לא הוי. תלי תנא דמתני' טעמא דלא יתנו משום מיתה, דאפילו מחיים נמי אין נותנין עד דלימא תנו. מדלא קתני "האומר כתבו גט (זה) לאשתי ומת, לא יתנו לאחר מיתה", ש"מ דאי אמר הכי, אפילו מחיים נמי לא יהבינן. ואי בשכיב מרע, אע"ג דלא אמר תנו אלא כתבו, יהבינן, כרבי שמעון שזורי:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:4.english: But he did not say "Give" - but [rather] said "Write," it is not [valid]. The Tanna of the Mishnah attributes the reason [that] "they should not give" [the get] to death, [whereas] even during his lifetime they do not give it until he says "Give." Since it does not teach: "One who says, 'Write this get for my wife,' and died, they should not give it after death," learn from this that if he said this, even during his lifetime we would not give it. And if [the case is] a deathbed [sick person], although he did not say "Give" but [only] "Write," we give it, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon Shezuri:

Rashi on Gittin 13b:4:1.english: One who goes out in a neck chain - To be executed.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:4:2.hebrew: ואמר כתבו גט לאשתי - כדי שלא תזקק ליבם:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:4:2.english: And he said: Write a bill of divorce for my wife - So that she will not be bound to a levir:

Rashi on Gittin 13b:4:3.hebrew: הרי אלו יכתבו ויתנו - דמתוך שהוא בהול על נפשו, לא גמר למילתי'. ומיהו, מכל מקום "כתבו ותנו" הוה דעתיה:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:4:3.english: These should write and give - For since he is panicked about his life, he did not complete his statement. But nevertheless, [by saying] "write," his intention was [also] "and give."

Rashi on Gittin 13b:4:4.english: One who sets sail - At sea.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:4:5.english: And one who departs in a caravan - [Who goes] to the desert.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:5:1.english: Even one who is dangerously ill - A person on his deathbed.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:6:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא - במלוה קנה, הא ליתא בעינא דלקנייה:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:6:1.english: What is the reason? - In the case of a loan, [the borrower] acquires [the money]; but it is not in existence in its original form for him to acquire it.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:8:1.hebrew: במילתי' דשמואל - גרסי' מי שאומר מלוה לי בידך:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:8:1.english: In the statement of Shmuel - We read [that one who says]: "A loan [is owed] to me in your possession."

Rashi on Gittin 13b:9:1.hebrew: נעשה כאומר לו - לוה אומר למלוה:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:9:1.english: It becomes like [one] who says to him - [Like] the borrower [who says] to the lender.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:9:2.english: At the time of the giving of the money - of the loan.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:9:3.hebrew: משעבדנא - מהשתא לכל מאן דאתי מחמתך. הלכך, כי א"ל תנהו לפלוני, איגלאי מילתא דמשעת מתן מעות אשתעבד ליה:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:9:3.english: I am beholden - From now [on], to anyone who comes by virtue of you. Therefore, when [the lender] says to [the borrower], "Give it to so-and-so," it becomes revealed [retroactively] that from the time of the giving of the money, [the borrower] became obligated to him.

Tosafot on Gittin 13b:10:1.hebrew: הקנה לנולדים הכי נמי דלא קנו - פי': הקנה לנולדים במעמד שלשה שלא נולדו עדיין בשעת מתן מעות, הכי נמי דלא קנו. ולספרים דגרסי "הכי נמי דקנו", הכי פי': הקנה לנולדים בקנין בעלמא בלא מעמד שלשה, דלא הוו בשעת קנין שלא נולדו עדיין, ה"נ דקנו, דהא במעמד שלשתן קנו אפי' נולדו אחרי כן:
Tosafot on Gittin 13b:10:1.english: "If he transferred to those who will be born, is it also so that they do not acquire?" - Explanation: [If] he transferred to those who will be born, in the presence of the three parties, who were not yet born at the time the money was given, is it also so that they do not acquire? But according to the texts that read, "is it also so that they acquire," this is the explanation: [If] he transferred to those who will be born by means of an ordinary act of acquisition, without the presence of the three parties, since they did not exist at the time of the act of acquisition, as they were not yet born, is it also so that they acquire? [This is a challenge,] for in the presence of the three parties they acquire, even if they were born afterward:

Tosafot on Gittin 13b:11:1.hebrew: לדבר שאינו בעולם מי אמר - הך סוגיא אליבא דרב הונא קיימא, דאית ליה שאדם מקנה דשלב"ל, ולא לדבר שלא בא לעולם. דבהאשה רבה (יבמות צג.) אית ליה גבי פירות דקל, משבאו לעולם אינו יכול לחזור בו. ובפרק מי שמת (ב"ב דף קמב.) קאמר רב הונא דהמזכה לעובר, אף לכשתלד לא קנה. ורב נחמן הוי איפכא מדרב הונא, דאית ליה התם: לכשתלד קנה; ובהאשה רבה (יבמות צג.) קאמר רב נחמן: אף משבאו לעולם יכול לחזור בו. וא"ת: מהיכא שמעינן ליה לר' מאיר דאדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם? היינו מההיא דקתני (שם צג:): "לאחר שתתגיירי ושתשתחררי — מקודשת". מההיא גופא שמעינן נמי דאדם מקנה לדבר שלא בא לעולם, דהא קתני: לאחר שאתגייר, לאחר שאשתחרר — דמקודשת. ויש לומר: דעובד כוכבים ועבד איתנהו בעולם, אלא שמחוסרים גירות ושחרור, ולא דמו לנולדים דליתנהו בעולם כלל. ואע"ג דילפינן מינה דאדם מקנה לר"מ פירות דקל, ולא מפלגינן — היינו משום דאית לן למימר דקאי בשיטתיה דרבי אלעזר בן יעקב, דאמר (קידושין סב:): האומר "פירות ערוגה זו מחוברין יהיו תרומה על פירות ערוגה זו התלושין, לכשיביאו שליש ויתלשו" — דבריו קיימין:
Tosafot on Gittin 13b:11:1.english: "To an entity that is not in the world — who said [that it is possible]?" - This passage stands according to Rav Huna, who holds that a person can transfer ownership of something that has not yet come into existence, but not to an entity that has not yet come into the world. For in [the chapter] Ha'isha Rabbah (Yevamot 93a) he holds, with regard to the fruit of a date palm, that once they have come into the world [the giver] cannot retract. And in the chapter Mi Shemet (Bava Batra 142a) Rav Huna says that one who grants [property] to an unborn child, even when [the child] is born, [the child] does not acquire it. And Rav Nachman is the reverse of Rav Huna, for there he holds: when [the child] is born, [the child] acquires it; and in Ha'isha Rabbah (Yevamot 93a) Rav Nachman says: even after [the fruits] have come into the world, [the giver] can retract. And if you will ask: From where do we learn that Rabbi Meir holds that a person can transfer ownership of something that has not yet come into the world? [One could answer:] from that [passage] where it teaches (ibid. 93b): "After you convert" or "after you are freed — she is betrothed." From that very [passage] we also learn that a person can transfer ownership to an entity that has not yet come into the world, for it teaches: after he converts, after he is freed — she is betrothed. And one can answer: a gentile and a slave exist in the world, but they lack conversion and manumission, and they are not comparable to those not yet born, who do not exist in the world at all. And although we derive from it that, according to Rabbi Meir, a person can transfer ownership of date-palm fruit, and we do not distinguish [between cases] — this is because we must say that he stands by the position of Rabbi Elazar ben Yaakov, who said (Kiddushin 62b): One who says, "The fruits of this attached bed shall be terumah for the fruits of this other bed that are detached, when they reach a third [of their growth] and are detached" — his words stand.

Tosafot on Gittin 13b:1:1.hebrew: קסבר רב פפא כי אמר רב לא שנא מלוה לא שנא פקדון - וא"ת: ולרב פפא, ורב גופיה אמאי לא אוקי מתני' במעמד שלשתן, ואפי' אין צבורין? וכי תימא: משום דלא משמע ליה לישנא דמתני' במעמד שלשתן — אם כן, מהאי טעמא הוה ליה למימר דרב פפא לא אמר כרב זביד. וי"ל: אע"ג דמתני' לא משמע ליה לרב במעמד ג', מ"מ מדאתא רב פפא לאיפלוגי ארב זביד, משמע שיש לו כח וטעם, דבשום ענין לא מפרשא מילתא דרב משום מעמד שלשתן:
Tosafot on Gittin 13b:1:1.english: "Rav Pappa holds that when Rav spoke, there is no difference between a loan and a deposit" - And if you ask: [According to] Rav Pappa, why did Rav himself not establish the Mishnah as [speaking of a transfer] in the presence of all three parties, even if the coins are not piled? And if you say [it is] because the wording of the Mishnah does not imply to him [a case of] "in the presence of the three of them" — if so, for this same reason Rav Pappa should have said that he does not speak in accordance with Rav Zevid. And one can answer: Although the Mishnah does not imply to Rav [a case of] the presence of three, nevertheless, since Rav Pappa came to disagree with Rav Zevid, it implies that he has a strong basis and reasoning, [namely] that in no way is the statement of Rav explained on account of [the principle of] presence of the three of them:

Tosafot on Gittin 13b:2:1.hebrew: ממאי מדקתני תנו ולא קתני כתבו - וא"ת: הא דקתני "תנו", אשמעי' דאפי' הכי אין כופין את היורשים לשחרר, כרבי דפליג בירושלמי אדרבנן, ואמר דתנו לא הוי כשיחררו אלא ככתבו, ואין כופין. וי"ל דמתני' לא אתא לאשמועינן בדין מצוה לקיים דברי המת אם כופין היורשים לקיים אם לאו, אלא לאשמועי' דאין גט לאחר מיתה. ועוד דמסתמא כרבנן אתיא:
Tosafot on Gittin 13b:2:1.english: "From where?" From the fact that it teaches "give" and does not teach "write" - And if you ask: [Perhaps] by teaching "give," it informs us that even so, the heirs are not compelled to free [the slave] — in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who disagrees with the Rabbis in the Yerushalmi, and says that "give" is not like "free him" but like "write," and [so] they are not compelled. And one can answer: The mishna did not come to teach us, regarding the law of the obligation to fulfill the words of the deceased, whether the heirs are compelled to fulfill [them] or not, but rather to teach us that there is no bill of divorce after death. Moreover, [the mishna] presumably follows the Rabbis:

Tosafot on Gittin 13b:7:1.hebrew: גופא אמר רב הונא אמר רב כו' תנהו לפלוני במעמד שלשתן קנה - אוריב"א וכן ר"ת, דבמעמד ג' קנה בעל כרחו של לוה או של נפקד. דאי לא קני אלא מרצונו, למאן דאמר דוקא בפקדון קנה, למה הוצרכו לתקן מעמד ג'? יאמר לו זכי! ואין נראה לומר דהוצרכו לתקן למקום שאין הפקדון ביד הנפקד אלא ביד אחרים, דלא יועיל אם יאמר זכי. ועוד, אף כשאין הפקדון ביד הנפקד יקנה באודיתא, כדאמר התם (ב"ב דף קמט.): אדהכי נפקא אודיתא מבי איסור גיורא. אלא נראה להם דאפי' בעל כרחו של נפקד קני. וכן גבי איסור גיורא, דקאמר רבא: היכי ליקנינהו רב מרי להני זוזי? אי במעמד ג' לא אזלינא — משמע דאם היה הולך היה קונה בע"כ. ואין לומר: אם היה הולך שם היה מתרצה, לפי שהיה מתבייש בפני איסור לומר: אין רצוני. דאם כן, בלא מעמד שלשתן הוה לי' למימר: לא אזילנא, שלא יאמר לו: זכה, כי מסתמא היה הפקדון ביד רבא. ומיהו לההוא טעמא דמפרש בסמוך, בההיא הנאה דקא משתניא ליה ממלוה כו', משמע דלא קני אלא מדעתו, אלא דבלאו הכי מפיק ליה מההוא טעמא:
Tosafot on Gittin 13b:7:1.english: "Now to the matter itself: Rav Huna said in the name of Rav, etc. 'Give it to so-and-so,' in the presence of the three of them — he acquires" - Ori"v'a, and so too Rabbeinu Tam [hold], that in the presence of three parties he acquires even against the will of the debtor or of the one holding the deposit. For if he acquired only with [the holder's] consent, then according to the one who says [this applies] specifically to a deposit, why did they need to institute [the rule of] the presence of three? [The owner] could simply say to him, "Acquire [it]!" And it does not seem right to say that they needed to institute it for a situation where the deposit is not in the hands of the holder but in the hands of others, so that it would not be effective if he were to say "Acquire [it]"; moreover, even when the deposit is not in the hands of the holder, he can acquire by means of a declaration [odita], as it says there (Bava Batra 149a): "In the meantime, a declaration emerged from the house of Isur the convert." Rather, it appears to them that he acquires even against the will of the holder. And so too regarding Isur the convert, where Rava said: "How can Rav Mari acquire these coins? If [it is] in the presence of three parties, I will not go" — this implies that had he gone, he would have acquired against his will. And one cannot say: "If he had gone there, he would have consented, because he would have been embarrassed before Isur to say, 'I do not wish it.'" For if so, [even] without the presence of the three of them he should have said, "I will not go," so that [Isur] would not say to him, "Acquire [it]," since presumably the deposit was in Rava's hands. However, according to that reason which [the Gemara] explains shortly, [namely] that benefit which he derives from [the transfer, as opposed to] a loan, etc., it implies that he acquires only with his consent, except that even without this, [the Gemara] derives it from that reason.

Tosafot on Gittin 13b:7:2.hebrew: תנהו לפלוני במעמד ג' קנה - אומר ר"ת: דאע"ג דהמוכר שטר חוב לחבירו וחזר ומחלו — מחול; מכר או נתן במתנה במעמד שלשתן — אינו יכול למחול. וכן משמע בפ"ב דקדושין (דף מח.), דקאמר: במלוה בשטר פליגי, בדשמואל — דמ"ד מקודשת, לית ליה דשמואל, ומר אית ליה דשמואל. ואיבעית אימא: כולי עלמא אית להו דשמואל, ובאשה סמכה דעתה קמיפלגי; מ"ד מקודשת סבר דסמכה דעתה, דלא שביק לדידה ומחיל לאחריני. וכי קאמר: במלוה על פה פליגי בדרב הונא אי קנה במעמד ג' במלוה — משמע דאי אית להו דרב הונא, אף במלוה, לכולי עלמא מקודשת. ואי יכול למחול, אמאי מקודשת למאן דאית ליה גבי מלוה בשטר דלא סמכה דעתה? ואמאי לא מסיק ואיבעית אימא: כולי עלמא קנה במלוה, אפילו מלוה על פה, ובאשה סמכה דעתה פליגי, כדמסיק אדשמואל אמלוה בשטר? אלא משמע דבמעמד שלשתן אינו יכול למחול. וא"ת: בפ' החובל (ב"ק דף פט.), גבי היא שחבלה באחרים, דפריך: ותזבין כתובתה בטובת הנאה, ומשני: כל לגבי בעלה ודאי מחלה. והשתא אכתי תמכור במעמד שלשתן, דאז לא תוכל למחול! דאע"ג דהבעל ודאי לא יתרצה, הא פרישית דאפי' בעל כרחו קני. ועוד: גבי שחבלה בבעלה, תמכור במעמד ג', דשם יתרצה הבעל כדי לגבות חבלתו! וכן בספ"ק דב"מ (דף יט:), גבי מצא שובר, דפריך: בזמן שהאשה מודה, אמאי יחזיר לבעל? ניחוש דלמא כתבה ליתן בניסן ולא נתנה עד תשרי כו'; ומשני: ש"מ איתא לדשמואל. והשתא ניחוש דלמא מכרה במעמד ג', דאינה יכולה למחול! וי"ל: דלא תקינו מעמד ג' בכתובה, דאפשר שלא תבא לידי גבייה לעולם. ועי"ל: דהתם גבי שובר אין לחוש כלל דשמא מכרה במעמד שלשתן: דאם אין עדים שמכרה, א"כ הבעל והאשה יכפרו המכירה; ואם יש עדים ואומרים שהבעל נתרצה, או אפילו שתק — ודאי השובר שקר; ואם מיחה, אז מוכח שהשובר אמת, וליכא למיחש דלמא כתבה ליתן בניסן כו':
Tosafot on Gittin 13b:7:2.english: "Give it to so-and-so" in the presence of three — he acquires - Rabbeinu Tam says: Although one who sells a promissory note to his fellow, and [the seller] then returns and forgives [the debtor], it is forgiven — [nevertheless, if] he sold it or gave it as a gift in the presence of the three parties, he cannot forgive. And so it implies in the second chapter of Kiddushin (48a), where it says: With regard to a loan [documented] by a note they disagree, about the [ruling of] Shmuel — for the one who says she is betrothed does not hold of Shmuel's [ruling], and the other holds of Shmuel's [ruling]. And if you wish, say: Everyone holds of Shmuel's [ruling], and they disagree about whether she has set her mind [to accept it]; the one who says she is betrothed holds that she has set her mind [to it], for [the lender] would not leave her and forgive others. And when [the Gemara] says: With regard to an oral loan they disagree about Rav Huna's [ruling], whether one acquires in the presence of three with a loan — this implies that if they hold of Rav Huna's [ruling], even for a loan, everyone [agrees] she is betrothed. But if [the lender] can forgive, why is she betrothed according to the one who holds so regarding a loan by a note, [given] that she has not set her mind [to it]? And why does [the Gemara] not conclude: And if you wish, say: Everyone [holds that] one acquires with a loan, even an oral loan, and they disagree about whether she has set her mind [to it], as it concludes regarding Shmuel [and] a loan by a note? Rather, it implies that in the presence of the three, he cannot forgive. And if you ask: In the chapter Hachovel (Bava Kamma 89a), regarding a woman who injured others, [the Gemara] asks: Let her sell her marriage contract for the [mere] benefit [of the right to collect], and answers: She would certainly forgive [it] to her husband. But now, let her still sell it in the presence of the three, for then she could not forgive! For although the husband would certainly not agree, I have already explained that [it is acquired] even against his will. Furthermore, regarding a woman who injured her husband, let her sell it in the presence of three, for there the husband would agree, in order to collect for his injury! And likewise at the end of the first chapter of Bava Metzia (19b), regarding one who found a receipt, where [the Gemara] asks: When the woman admits, why should [the finder] return it to the husband? Let us suspect that perhaps she wrote [a receipt] to pay in Nisan but did not pay until Tishrei, etc.; and answers: Learn from this that [the Gemara] holds of Shmuel's [ruling]. But now, let us suspect that perhaps she sold it in the presence of three, [in which case] she cannot forgive! And one can answer: They did not institute [acquisition] in the presence of three for a marriage contract, for it is possible that she will never come to collect. And furthermore, one can say: There, regarding a receipt, there is no reason to suspect at all that perhaps she sold it in the presence of the three: for if there are no witnesses that she sold it, then the husband and the wife would deny the sale; and if there are witnesses and they say that the husband agreed, or even that he was silent — the receipt is certainly false; and if he protested, then it is evident that the receipt is true, and there is no need to suspect that perhaps she wrote [it] to pay in Nisan, etc.:

Tosafot on Gittin 13b:7:3.hebrew: במעמד שלשתן קנה - אומר ר"ת דלא תקינו מעמד שלשתן בעובד כוכבים. אם הנפקד או הלוה עובד כוכבים, ואמר ליה ישראל: תנהו לישראל אחר — לא קנה. כיון דאפילו אמר לו "זכי" לא קנה, כיון דאין זכיה לעובד כוכבים, ה"ה במעמד ג' לא קנה. ואם המקבל עובד כוכבים, ואמר ישראל לישראל: תנהו לפלוני עובד כוכבים, כל זמן שאינו חוזר בו יתן, אפי' אמר ליה בלא מעמד ג'. אבל אם חוזר בו, לא יתן לעובד כוכבים, אפי' אם אמר לו במעמד ג', אם לא שאינו יכול להשמט מן העובד כוכבים. ואם הנותן עובד כוכבים, נראה דקנה, דאם ממונו של ישראל הפקיעו על ידי מעמד ג' דהוי הלכתא בלא טעמא, כל שכן ממון העובד כוכבים. ועוד, דבדיניהם דיינינן ליה, שאמרינן לו לעובד כוכבים: כך דינכם, כדאמרי' בהגוזל בתרא (ב"ק קיג.):
Tosafot on Gittin 13b:7:3.english: "In the presence of the three of them, he has acquired" - Rabbeinu Tam says that [the Rabbis] did not institute [the rule of] presence of the three parties in the case of a gentile. If the bailee or the debtor is a gentile, and an Israelite said to him, "Give it to another Israelite," [the recipient] has not acquired it. Since even if he said to him "acquire [it]" [the recipient] has not acquired, because there is no [legal] agency of acquisition on behalf of [another through] a gentile, the same applies to the presence of the three parties — he has not acquired. And if the recipient is a gentile, and an Israelite said to another Israelite, "Give it to so-and-so, a gentile," as long as [the owner] has not retracted, he must give it, even if [the owner] said it to him without the presence of the three parties. But if [the owner] retracts, he should not give it to the gentile, even if [the owner] said it to him in the presence of the three parties, unless he cannot escape [the claim] from the gentile. And if the giver is a gentile, it appears that [the recipient] has acquired; for if the property of an Israelite is removed from his ownership through the presence of the three parties, which is a halakhah without a reason, all the more so the property of a gentile. Furthermore, we judge him according to their own laws, as we say to the gentile, "This is your law," as we say in [the chapter] Hagozel Batra (Bava Kamma 113a):
